### Exercise 2

<details><summary>**2.** Check whether this appears to be the most recent version of Pandoc</summary>
Version 2.14 is [not nearly the most recent one](https://pandoc.org/releases.html),
which is 3.8 as of September 2025.
</p></details>

<details><summary>**3.** Is a more recent Pandoc version available in an OSC module?</summary>

Yes:
   
```bash

```
```bash-out
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    Versions:
        pandoc/2.19.2
        pandoc/3.6.4
```
</details>

<details><summary>**4.** Load the module with the most recent available Pandoc version</summary>

</details>
   
<details><summary>**6.** Was a PDF file created?</summary>

If all went well, Pandoc did not print anything to screen,
but the PDF file should be there:

```bash
ls
```
```bash-out
data    README.md   README.pdf    results
```

</details>

<details><summary>**7.** Install the Papyrus PDF Preview and open the file.</summary>

1. Click on the Extensions icons (four squares) in the narrow side bar to open 
   the Extensions panel in the wide side bar.

2. Search for "papyrus" (or similar) and the extension should pop up:

![](../img/vscode_pdf-extension.png){width="60%" fig-align="center" fig-alt="A screenshot of the search result for the Papyrus PDF Preview VS Code extension."}

3. Click "Install".

4. After installation, you should be able to open the PDF file e.g. by simply
   clicking on it in the VS Code file explorer.

</details>

<details><summary>**8.** Download the PDF file</summary>

- Recall that in the VS Code file explorer, you can right-click on a file and
  select "Download..." to download a file to your computer.
  
- Alternatively, you could do this in the OnDemand file explorer.

</details>

#### X

<details><summary> The `printline.sh` script _(Click to expand)_</summary>
```bash
#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail

# Check the number of command-line arguments
if [[ ! "$#" -eq 2 ]]; then
    echo "Error: wrong number of arguments"
    echo "You provided $# arguments, while 2 are required."
    echo "Usage: printline.sh <file> <line-number>"
    exit 1
fi

# Copy the command-line arguments
input_file=$1
line_nr=$2

# Only print the requested line
head -n "$line_nr" "$input_file" | tail -n 1
```
</details>

<details><summary> Running and testing the script _(Click to expand)_</summary>

- To run the script and make it print the 4^th^ line of the Garrigos et al. metadata file:

  ```bash
  bash scripts/printline.sh garrigos-data/meta/metadata.tsv 4
  ```
  ```{.bash-out}
  ERR10802879     10dpi   cathemerium
  ```

- Or the 7^th^ line:

  ```bash
  bash scripts/printline.sh garrigos-data/meta/metadata.tsv 7
  ```
  ```{.bash-out}
  ERR10802884     10dpi   control
  ```

- To test that the check for the correct number of arguments works:

  ```bash
  # Only pass 1 argument:
  bash scripts/printline.sh garrigos-data/meta/metadata.tsv
  ```
  ```bash-out
  Error: wrong number of arguments
  You provided 1 arguments, while 2 are required
  Usage printline.sh <file> <line-number>
  ```
  
  ```bash
  # Pass 3 arguments:
  bash scripts/printline.sh garrigos-data/meta/metadata.tsv 4 7
  ```
  ```bash-out
  Error: wrong number of arguments
  You provided 3 arguments, while 2 are required
  Usage printline.sh <file> <line-number>
  ```

</details>
